Side out

Welcome to my blog about how I work and study the game. Everything is organized to save time and give you something clear and visual, even if it took quite a bit of time to build. Where data meets decision-making!

Let’s start by talking about what is probably the most studied phase by coaches : the opponent’s SIDE-OUT. And you, how do you study it?

How the opponent team attack on Side out ? Performance and Efficiency!

Distribution according on :

  • Where the ball comes from
  • The moment of the set
Blue = DistributionBlack = Performance Attack

How to study the game of the setter ?

  • With a lot of filter :
    • Rotation, Opponent rotation
    • Difference of score
    • Moment in the set
    • Quality of pass before
    • Netzone
    • Call

FLOW ?

With this table, the possibility to check for each attacker the amount and the performance.

  • You can filter by :
    • Who pass ?
    • Who defense ?
    • First Ball Side Out / Break Point ?
    • And you can combine these with the filters we mentioned earlier!

Study our own Team

You probably have things to fix in your team!

This chart helps us to understand how our team is progressing. By comparing the two periods, game by game or set by set. Here ? We can see the first five games versus the last five games played.

It’s always useful to evaluate the other teams in the league to understand where we stand.

How should we evaluate our players and assess their performance?

  • Checking by skill
  • Amount
  • Performance

Serve and Pass

Quality of Pass according on where the serve come from! Possible to filter the type of the Serve, Rotation, Receiver.

How to improve the serve ?

  • Checking for the Team and by Player the strentgh and the weakness.
  • Some favorite direction ?
  • If for the next game you need to change your Serve ?
  • The Serve, influence your decision for the Match-Up ?

CF = coefficient ? How many mistakes I need to collect one ace ? or How many serves I need to collect one serve out of system ?

  • Where do my players serve?
  • Where do they perform best in %?
  • Where do they perform best in terms of aces?
🎯

This chart helps us understand, with the additional filters applied, in which contact zones our players perform the best.

This gives us clear areas of focus both for improving our own reception and for serving strategies aimed at weakening the opponent’s reception.
